defects.claim: "Nancy R. Peck's feature ... dated the first issue to June 1882, twenty years of publication ending with his death in 1901 at 65."
defects.problem: The 1993 article never says Smith died at 65. It says he was 65 four years before his death, which puts his age at death at 69 — the same age The Record gives. The event states a false fact about the source.
defects.evidence: Opened data/research/newspapers-com/downloads/sunday-news-ridgewood_1993-06-27_p2_smallest-newspaper.jpg (col. 4): "At the age of 65, four years before his death in 1901, Smith wrote, 'As people search its pages for a name, a date or an event of which The Landscape contains the only record, someone may say: I knew the editor.'" 1832 birth + 65 = 1897; 1897 + 4 = 1901 death at 69.

defects.claim: "The Sunday News says he died in 1901 at age 65." — offered as a disclosed conflict with The Record's age 69.
defects.problem: The conflict is manufactured. The 1993 Sunday News is consistent with age 69 at death, not 65. The disclosure misrepresents the source and preserves a nonexistent discrepancy in the archive's confidence rating ("medium").
defects.evidence: Same 1993 JPG passage read above: "At the age of 65, four years before his death in 1901." The Record image (the-record-hackensack_1991-02-09_p2_landscape-renamed.jpg) reads: "ceasing publication in July 1901. Smith died four months later, at the age of 69." Both sources agree on 69.

defects.claim: "Smith bought a printing press and began publishing A.P. Smith's Paper" — dated May 1881, citing the 1991 Record among its sources.
defects.problem: The cited Record source dates the press purchase to the late 1870s, several years before the paper. Folding the press purchase into the May 1881 first-issue date contradicts the source it cites.
defects.evidence: the-record-hackensack_1991-02-09_p2_landscape-renamed.jpg: "In the late 1870s, Smith bought a printing press and began a printing business that he operated out of his house. Several years later, he started publishing The Landscape." The Ridgewood News image supports only "printed ... from May of 1881," not a press purchase in 1881.

defects.claim: "After his father died, Alfred P. Smith opened a job-printing shop on East Allendale Road."
defects.problem: No source places the 1876 job-printing shop on East Allendale Road. The 1987 article attaches East Allendale Road to the house where the newspaper sheets were printed, not to the shop; The Record says the printing business ran out of his house and places that house on Chestnut Ridge Road. The street is an inference presented as reported fact.
defects.evidence: ridgewood-news_1987-11-26_p14_landscape-ap-smith.jpg: "the 9- by 15- sheets were printed by Smith himself in a house that still exists on East Allendale Road from May of 1881 until July of 1901" and separately "He started a job-printing business in 1876 after his father died" — no address. The Record image: "born in 1832 in Saddle River, in a small house on what is now Chestnut Ridge Road" and "a printing business that he operated out of his house."

defects.claim: "The paper died with him in 1901."
defects.problem: States a contested causal sequence as settled. The Record reverses it: the paper stopped first and Smith died four months afterward. evt-017 discloses this conflict, but the story thread resolves it silently in favor of one source.
defects.evidence: the-record-hackensack_1991-02-09_p2_landscape-renamed.jpg: "The Landscape was part of Bergen County life for 20 years, ceasing publication in July 1901. Smith died four months later, at the age of 69." Only ridgewood-news_1987-11-26 supports the simultaneity: "when he died, the paper ceased publishing."

defects.claim: "born in Saddle River in 1832 to a family descended from enslaved people"
defects.problem: The descent claim rests on a 1993 article quoting a January 1992 historical-society newsletter — third-hand, and it describes Smith personally, not his family line. The only source that describes his family says his father was a laborer who owned a small farm and says nothing about enslavement. The thread presents it as an established birth fact.
defects.evidence: sunday-news-ridgewood_1993-06-27_p2_smallest-newspaper.jpg: "As noted in the Upper Saddle River Historical Society's newsletter of January 1992, 'A.P. Smith was a remarkable man, the descendant of slaves, who was educated and well-respected throughout the region.'" the-record-hackensack_1991-02-09: "His father, once a laborer, owned a small farm there."

defects.claim: "Between April and June 1891 Smith used The Landscape to push for paving Saddle River's roads. The vote carried and $2,000 was appropriated."
defects.problem: The source dates no part of the paving campaign except a single April 1891 quote and gives no date for the vote. The June 1891 tag in the article belongs to the suburban-growth prediction, a separate quote, so the April–June window for the paving push is constructed, not reported.
defects.evidence: ridgewood-news_1987-11-26_p14_landscape-ap-smith.jpg: the macadam quote ends "(April, 1891)"; the next sentence, "The vote to pave was carried and $2,000 was appropriated to begin the work," carries no date; a later quote about "a great wave of city people ... rolling over Bergen county" ends "(June, 1891)"; an intervening quote is tagged "(Feb. 1890)," so the column is not in chronological order.

defects.claim: "Newark buried him with the state's Black political leadership as pallbearers."
defects.problem: The funeral was in Trenton, not Newark. The only cited source places every element of the service in Trenton.
defects.evidence: Opened C:/Users/Joe Amditis/Desktop/Crimes/playground/njblackpress/data/research/newspapers-com/downloads/new-york-age_1909-10-21_p1_herbert-obituary.jpg (page 1, col. 5). Text: "TRENTON, N. J., October 19.—Funeral services were held last Saturday over the remains of the late R. Henri Herbert... Services were held at the late residence, 25 Lambertson street, at 1 o'clock, and at Mt. Zion A. M. E. Church at 2 o'clock. Rev. H. B. Anderson officiated." and "The remains were interred in Riverview Cemetery." Newark appears only as the home city of some honorary pallbearers and of "out-of-town friends" (Mrs. James Baxter and Mrs. James Wormley, Newark). Honorary pallbearers were mostly out-of-state: Fred R. Moore, George S. Douglas, D. S. Willie, Robert R. Willis, John T. Lewis and M. P. Launders of New York; Chris Perry of Philadelphia; William S. Powell of Camden.

defects.claim: "Herbert's funeral in Newark is dated Saturday, October 23, 1909" / "gave the funeral as Saturday, October 23, in Newark."
defects.problem: Both the date and the city are wrong. The article is datelined Trenton, October 19 and reports a funeral already held "last Saturday" — October 16, 1909. October 23 appears nowhere in the article; it was inferred from the "FUNERAL SATURDAY" deck by assuming the Saturday after the October 21 press date.
defects.evidence: Opened new-york-age_1909-10-21_p1_herbert-obituary.jpg. Masthead: "NEW YORK, THURSDAY, OCTOBER 21, 1909." Story dateline: "TRENTON, N. J., October 19.—Funeral services were held last Saturday..." With an October 19 dateline, "last Saturday" is October 16. Venue text: 25 Lambertson street and Mt. Zion A. M. E. Church, interment Riverview Cemetery — all Trenton.

defects.claim: "Sources conflict on whether this is an announcement or a report... An October 21 press date cannot witness an October 23 event... Do not treat the funeral as independently confirmed until a later issue is read."
defects.problem: The disclosed conflict does not exist in the artifact. The article is unambiguously a retrospective report of a completed funeral, datelined six days after the death and three days after the service. The caution rests entirely on the fabricated October 23 date, so it misdirects future researchers.
defects.evidence: Opened new-york-age_1909-10-21_p1_herbert-obituary.jpg. Past-tense reporting throughout: "Funeral services were held last Saturday"; "many prominent members of the race attended the funeral"; "Rev. H. B. Anderson officiated"; "The remains were interred in Riverview Cemetery"; "Several carriages were required to carry the numerous floral tributes to the grave"; "Numerous places of business... remained closed until after the funeral."

defects.claim: "...and joining the Republican State Committee in 1895."
defects.problem: He did not join the committee. The same article the thread relies on states that committee membership could not be conferred except by the delegate convention, so the committee instead invited him to attend meetings for consultation and advice. "Joining" erases the distinction the source draws deliberately. Note evt-015 states this correctly ("consulting member"); only the thread overstates it.
defects.evidence: Opened C:/Users/Joe Amditis/Desktop/Crimes/playground/njblackpress/data/research/newspapers-com/downloads/trenton-sunday-advertiser_1895-10-20_p1_herbert-gop-committee.jpg, p1: subhead "Appointed as a Consulting Member of the Republican State Committee"; body: "...reported that under the rules of the party membership on the State Committee could only be conferred by the convention called to elect delegates to the National Convention, but..."; resolution: "That Mr. R. Henri Herbert be invited to attend all meetings of the State Committee for the purpose of consultation and advice..."

defects.claim: "...the son of Mansfield Herbert, who escaped slavery, bought his family's freedom..."
defects.problem: "His family's freedom" misstates who was purchased. The source names himself, his father, and his sister — not a wife or children. evt-001 states this correctly; the thread's compression is looser than the record.
defects.evidence: Opened new-york-tribune_1895-12-08_p14_herbert-profile.jpg, p14: "...before he was thirty years of age had purchased freedom for himself, his father and sister, paying to his former owners over $3,000..."

defects.problem: The 1882 end date contradicts the only cited source for the paper's life, which gives a three-year run from 1880 and a sale (not a cessation) to Colonel E. C. Stahl, who consolidated it with The Trenton Herald. evt-004 follows the source; the publication record does not.

C. Stahl and consolidated with 'The Trenton Herald.'" Three years from 1880 ends about 1883, and the title continued inside the Herald.

defects.location: data/research/editorial/events.json evt-007 (description, "the New York Evening World's")

defects.problem: The scan is Joseph Pulitzer's morning paper The World, not The Evening World. The event, the reading log, and the file slug all carry the wrong title.

defects.location: data/research/editorial/events.json evt-007 (description, "body text is too degraded to transcribe, so the paper referred to is unconfirmed")
defects.claim: The squib body cannot be read, so the publication it refers to is unconfirmed and rests only on the file slug; confidence "medium".
defects.problem: The item is fully legible and carries an explicit credit line naming the New Jersey Trumpet. The attribution is not an inference from the filename, and the recorded uncertainty is false.
defects.evidence: Cropped the same JPG at x1580-2050, y2340-2900 and read it at 2x. It reads in full: "A Roaring Jersey Negro Editor. [From the New Jersey Trumpet—Negro Organ.] The Southern white man has the same contempt, hatred and enmity to the black man to-day as he had before the 'wah.' He would enslave us to-morrow had he the power. Again would he prostitute our mothers and our sisters, again would he sell our brothers and his own flesh and blood in the public squares as he did thirty years ago, if it were not for the ballots which we now cast. Better a thousand times we should be exterminated than surrender one single right so dearly purchased." The item is a reprint from the Trumpet, not a report about an unidentified paper.

defects.location: data/research/editorial/events.json evt-011 (description, "The Daily Press put attendance at about 100; the Shore Press put it at about 500.")
defects.claim: The two papers gave conflicting attendance figures for the Marrow's Hall meeting.
defects.problem: There is no conflict. Both papers print the identical sentence, and the 100 and 500 are sequential counts within that one sentence (8 o'clock arrivals vs. the later crowd), not competing estimates by two outlets. The Shore Press is a reprint of the Daily's account.
defects.evidence: Opened asbury-park-press_1893-07-22_p1_murrell-speaking.jpg (crop x60-560, y1000-1450): "At 8 o'clock about 100 people had assembled, but as the news spread that speakers were actually in attendance and that the idea of a meeting had assumed tangible shape, a crowd numbering nearly 500 crowded into the little room and clustered around the open doors and windows." Opened shore-press_1893-07-28_p6_murrell-asbury-meeting.jpg (crop x60-640, y540-1000): word-for-word the same sentence, and the Shore Press column is tagged "From Saturday's DAILY." above it.

defects.claim: "Murrell enters his federal office" on 1889-05-25.
defects.problem: The only source is dated 1889-05-18 and reports a future intention. A newspaper of May 18 cannot witness May 25. The event title states as fact something the record only announces; the hedge survives only in the description.
defects.evidence: Opened washington-bee_1889-05-18_p2_murrell-trumpet-editor.jpg (crop x1250-1700, y1600-2600), item headed "AS THE BEE PREDICTED": "As we predicted last week, Col. Wm. Murrell editor of the New Jersey TRUMPET would be appointed, Col. Murrell received his commission on Wednesday and will enter upon the duties of his new office on the 25th." No later source in data/research/editorial/readings/ confirms he took office.

defects.location: data/research/editorial/events.json evt-007 (description, quoted headline and column name)
defects.claim: The item is headed "A Roaring New Jersey Negro Editor" and sits in the "Squibs from the Squibs" column.
defects.problem: Both quoted strings are wrong. The headline omits "New," and the column standing head is "SQUIBS FROM THE SQUIBOBS." The Trumpet excerpt also sits below the squib run, set off by its own rule, rather than inside it.
defects.evidence: Same JPG. Crop x1580-2060, y1900-2400 shows the standing head "SQUIBS FROM THE SQUIBOBS." followed by one-line exchanges credited to Toledo Blade, Washington Post, Harper's Weekly, Pittsburg Chronicle, Boston Gazette, Merchant Traveller, Somerville Journal, Baltimore American, Terre Haute Express. A printer's rule then separates the standalone piece headed "A Roaring Jersey Negro Editor."

defects.location: data/research/editorial/stories.json story-003 (thread, "edited by Rev. Fillmore Smith to cover that community directly")
defects.claim: The Monmouth edition was created and edited by Fillmore Smith in order to cover the Monmouth County Black community directly.
defects.problem: The source states only who edited the Monmouth edition. The stated purpose is the writer's inference. evt-012's "edited the Monmouth edition locally" adds the same unsupported locality detail.
defects.evidence: Opened shore-press_1893-07-28_p6_murrell-asbury-meeting.jpg (crop x1090-1560, y2960-3120). Full notice: "The first issue of the Monmouth edition of the New Jersey Trumpet has just reached this office. The Trumpet is published by Colonel William Murrell at Newark, in the interests of the colored race. The Monmouth edition is edited by Rev. Fillmore Smith, D. D." The "in the interests of the colored race" phrase describes the parent Trumpet, not the Monmouth edition's remit, and no purpose or place of editing is given.

defects.location: data/research/editorial/stories.json story-003 (thread, closing line "The paper followed the fight.")
defects.claim: The Monmouth edition was launched in response to the Asbury Park pavilion fight.
defects.problem: A causal claim the sources cannot carry. The Shore Press only records that a first issue reached its office on 1893-07-28; a weekly edition printed and delivered within seven days of the meeting is at least as consistent with prior planning. The thread concedes the launch date is undocumented, then asserts the causation anyway.
defects.evidence: Same Shore Press notice (crop above) gives no launch date, no prospectus, and no reference to the meeting. The only other Trumpet Monmouth reference in data/research/editorial/readings/ is this one file; readings/ contains no earlier or later notice of the edition.

defects.location: data/research/editorial/stories.json thread story-004, lines 75 and 77 (and events.json evt-019, lines 300 and 302)
defects.claim: The Echo's editor was "W. E. Rack," listed as a person distinct from the 1904 co-editor "Rock."
defects.problem: The name is wrong. The 1909 clipping prints "W. E. Rock" twice, and the project's own publication record (id 31) names him "Rock, William E." / "William Elijah Rock." The misspelling also splits one man into two people in the thread's people array ("W. E. Rack" plus "Rock") and hides the actual continuity: the Rock of "Rock & Howard" in 1904 is the same W. E. Rock who moved the paper in 1909.
defects.evidence: Opened data/research/newspapers-com/downloads/asbury-park-press_1909-03-05_p2_echo-moves-red-bank.jpg (crop x480-840, y3190-3560). Text reads: "ECHO MOVES TO RED BANK. The Echo, edited and published in the interest of the colored race in Long Branch by W. E. Rock for the past five years, has moved to Red Bank, where Editor Rock has purchased a home." Both instances are "Rock," not "Rack." data/publications.json id 31 keyStaff: "Rock, William E."; data/research/source-catalog.json quote for this clipping also reads "by W. E. Rock." The error originates in readings/asbury-park-press_1909-03-05_p2_echo-moves-red-bank.json, which mis-transcribed it as Rack.

defects.location: data/research/editorial/stories.json thread story-004, line 75 (and events.json evt-018, line 282)
defects.claim: "A suspected arson fire gutted its press room in 1904"; event title: "Fire destroys the Echo's press room in Long Branch."
defects.problem: "Gutted" and "destroys" overstate the source. The Monmouth Democrat reports damage "to the extent of several hundred dollars" — a modest sum — and says only that the paper was "burned out." Nothing supports destruction or gutting of the press room.
defects.evidence: Opened data/research/newspapers-com/downloads/monmouth-democrat_1904-09-08_p4_echo-burned-out.jpg (col. 2, y~3434-3700). Full item: "Colored Newspaper Burned Out. The Echo, a weekly negro newspaper published at Long Branch, was burned out recently. The fire which is thought to be of incendiary origin damaged the machinery and press-room of the newspaper to the extent of several hundred dollars. The first issue of the paper was edited by Rock & Howard."

defects.location: data/research/editorial/stories.json thread story-004, line 75 (and events.json evt-019, line 300)
defects.claim: Rock moved the paper "after buying a home there and planning an industrial school"; event: "Rack planned to run an industrial school in Red Bank."
defects.problem: The clipping says he will HELP run an industrial school, not that he planned or would run one. The thread and event both promote him from participant to principal.
defects.evidence: Same 1909 image, continuation crop (y3190-3560): "While in Long Branch he has done good work toward elevating his race. He wll help run an industrial school for his race at Red Bank."

defects.location: data/research/editorial/stories.json thread story-004, line 75 (and events.json evt-022, line 347)
defects.claim: "By 1921 the New York Age was reprinting Red Bank Echo items"; event title: "The New York Age reprints an item from the Red Bank Echo."
defects.problem: The Age did not reprint an Echo item. Its editorial press-comment column ran a single one-sentence summary of what the Echo had itself cited. Calling it reprinting (and, in the event, a "clippings column") overstates the exchange relationship the thread rests its conclusion on.
defects.evidence: Opened data/research/newspapers-com/downloads/new-york-age_1921-04-09_p4_red-bank-echo-cited.jpg, right rail (x2170-2500, y240-3100). The paragraph reads: "The Red Bank Echo cites a rare case of the disease known as cornucornutum in Baltimore, the subject being a colored man who had a five inch horn removed from his forehead. This throws the cases of encephalitis lethargica in the shade as a distinctive malady." Neighboring paragraphs in the same column are the Age's own commentary on the Detroit Leader, the Christian Recorder, the Beaumont (Tex.) Monitor, the Galveston City Times, and the Norfolk Journal and Guide — a press-comment roundup, not reprinted copy.

defects.claim: Title: "The Echo survives a fire and moves down the shore."
defects.problem: The geography is backwards. Red Bank is inland and north-west of Long Branch, on the Navesink River, roughly eight miles off the ocean. Moving from Long Branch to Red Bank is moving away from the shore, not "down the shore" (which in New Jersey usage means toward the coast).
defects.evidence: The 1909 clipping (opened, above) states the move is from Long Branch to Red Bank. The publication record data/publications.json id 31 gives city as "Long Branch/Red Bank." No source describes a move along or toward the shore.

defects.claim: "By 1942 it printed from 130 W. Kinney St., the Herald's old address."
defects.problem: 130 W. Kinney St. was never the Newark Herald's address. The Newark Herald printed from 152 West Kinney Street. And 130 W. Kinney St. was the New Jersey Herald News's own office from its third issue, weeks before any merger — so the address proves nothing about absorption and the causal implication of the sentence is false.

(Incorporated) / 152 West Kinney St. ... Telephone MArket 3-0940 / NEWARK, N. J." and "Address all communications and make all checks payable to The Newark Herald, 152 West Kinney Street, Newark, N. J." Opened data/research/ia/clean/NewJerseyHeraldNews19380521a.pdf p.4 masthead (Vol. 1, No. 3, May 21, 1938): "New Jersey Herald News / Office — 130 W. Kinney St., Newark, N. J. Telephone MA 2-9799." Opened NewJerseyHeraldNews19390311.pdf p.1 nameplate: "OFFICE: 130 W. KINNEY ST., NEWARK / TELEPHONE: MArket 2-9799." Opened NewJerseyHeraldNews19420704.pdf p.8 masthead: "130 West Kinney Street, Newark, N. J."

defects.claim: The March 11, 1939 front-page series "promis[ed] Jersey City the following week."
defects.problem: The paper promised Paterson, not Jersey City. The only Jersey City item on that front page is an unrelated story about Dr. A. W. Johnson qualifying as a specialist.
defects.evidence: Opened data/research/ia/clean/NewJerseyHeraldNews19390311.pdf. Page 1 box reads "Obstacles Faced By The Race In NEWARK — (This is the first of a series of facts to be published about the conditions affecting Negroes in various municipalities of New Jersey.)" with "(Continued on Page 2)." Rendered page 2 at 400 dpi: the article ends "SUMMARY ... shockingly deprived of representation on policy-fixing boards." followed by the tagline "(NEXT WEEK: PATERSON)".

defects.claim: "the June 11, 1938 Newark Herald scan (evt-028) shows the same W. Kinney St. address in use by the Newark Herald Publishing Co."
defects.problem: The addresses are not the same. The 1938 Newark Herald masthead gives 152 West Kinney Street; the 1942 Herald News gives 130 West Kinney Street. Different buildings on the same street, and different phone numbers (MArket 3-0940 vs MArket 2-9799). The clause is offered as corroborating context for the merger and does not corroborate it.

defects.problem: The masthead initial is E., not F. The event resolves two other OCR name errors from this same log but carries this third one through unflagged.

defects.claim: "either the suspension was temporary or the volume count predates the 1928 start implied here."
defects.problem: The second alternative is refuted by primary sources already in this batch, and the arithmetic does not support it. Volume 11 in 1938 is exactly what a 1928 first volume produces. The 1928 start is not merely "implied" — two mastheads state it outright. The event also omits that the 1932 item itself predicted resumption, which is what actually resolves the puzzle.

Editor Clark has moved his office from the well known Cotton Building and while no statement has been made, it is expected that he will receive the necessary backing for its resumption." Opened NewarkHerald19380611a.pdf p.6 masthead: "Entered as second class matter May 4, 1928 at the Post Office at Newark, N. J." Opened NewJerseyHeraldNews19420704.pdf p.8 masthead: "Established 1928 as Newark Herald."

defects.claim: the New Jersey Herald News was "printing the motto 'Owned and Published by New Jersey Negroes.'"
defects.problem: That line is the ownership ear box at the right of the nameplate, not the paper's motto. The motto is carried on the eagle ribbon inside the nameplate and reads differently. The reading log distinguishes the two; the story collapses them.
defects.evidence: Opened data/research/ia/clean/NewarkHerald19380611a.pdf p.13 (New Jersey Herald News, Vol. 1, No. 6) rendered at 420 dpi. The right-hand box reads "Owned and Published By New Jersey Negroes"; the ribbon under the flag reads "EQUALITY · JUSTICE · OPPORTUNITY · FOR THE NEGRO PEOPLE". The reading log NewarkHerald19380611a.json also lists them separately: "'Owned and Published by New Jersey Negroes,' motto 'Equality Justice Opportunity for the Negro People'."

defects.claim: "In 1932 the Afro-American reported the Newark Herald had folded after four years."
defects.problem: The source says more than four years, not four. The compression matters here because the thread then treats the Volume 11 numbering in 1938 as a puzzle, and the extra months are part of what reconciles it with the 1928 founding.
defects.evidence: Opened afro-american_1932-07-09_p7_newark-herald-folded.jpg at full resolution: "The paper has been regularly published more than four years and its demise is keenly felt by the entire state." evt-024 renders this correctly as "more than four years"; the story drops the qualifier.

defects.claim: "Mrs. Elizabeth Mitchell was reinstated" as a Douglass Park attendant after the Third Ward protest.
defects.problem: The wrong woman is named as the reinstated attendant. Elizabeth Mitchell led the protest group; the attendant returned to her job was Mrs. Carrie Bartee. Two other dismissed women (Mrs. Grace Bell, Mrs. Dorothy Hynes) were still out.

Recommendation: merge id 24 into id 9, keep 1928-1939, keep OCLC 2696527 / LCCN sn88071222, drop the 1938 founding and the 1999 end year, and park LCCN 2012210650 on id 9 as an unverified second catalog record. id 24 also carries isFeaturedHistoric true while absent from featured-publications.json, so it is an orphan that inflates the 137 total and the featured set.
defects.evidence: (1) Both records carry the same OCLC number 2696527. (2) data/research/source-catalog.json ids 9 and 24 hold byte-identical evidence: the same 5 newspapers.com cards (all for a white Newark, Nebraska paper) and the same 12 Internet Archive issues; id 24's row has no LCCN at all ("no LCCN in record"). (3) A 1938 founding is impossible: rendered NewarkHerald19380611a.pdf page 1 reads "VOL. 11, No. 18 ... SATURDAY, JUNE 11, 1938", which back-dates the founding to about 1928, matching id 9. (4) The 1999 end year has no support and is contradicted by rendered NewJerseyHeraldNews19390311.pdf page 1: "Herald News Combined with THE NEWARK HERALD", VOL. XII, No. 5, March 11, 1939. (5) id 24 has null missionStatement, null historicalNotes, null websiteUrl and a guessed publisher "New Jersey Herald News Pub. Co. (related to Herald-Advance lineage)", while the June 11, 1938 masthead names Newark Herald Publishing Co.

defects.claim: July 23 log: publication "New Jersey Herald News (Newark Herald)", "Vol. 11, No. 23 ... 20-page issue". July 30 log: same conflated title string.
defects.problem: The July 23 scan is two papers bound together, not one 20-page issue: Newark Herald Vol. 11 No. 23 on pages 1-12 and New Jersey Herald News Vol. 1 No. 12 on pages 13-20. The log merges them under one hyphenated title, which is how the Elizabeth pool and Federation convention items ended up attributed to publication id 16 in events.json (evt-039, evt-041). The July 30 scan is Herald-only and should not carry the Herald News name at all.
defects.evidence: Rendered NewarkHerald19380723a.pdf page 13: "NEW JERSEY Herald News", Vol. 1, No. 12, week ending Saturday, July 23, 1938, lead "RACE BAN CLOSES POOL". Rendered NewarkHerald19380730a.pdf page 1: "The Newark Herald", VOL. 11, No. 24, 12 PAGES. grep of both .txt files returns zero occurrences of "Herald News" in the Herald pages. The 0611 and 0702 logs correctly describe the same bundling pattern ("bound with", "two distinct Newark Black weeklies"), so 0723 and 0730 are the outliers.
